title: Non-small cell lung cancer
subtitle: Adenocarcinoma · squamous · large cell · TNM 9th edition (Jan 2025) · the driver landscape moves faster than any printed card — re-check NCCN at every new diagnosis
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, NSCLC (Salter A, Roy M) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Chest CT with contrast (nodes are far easier to call with contrast)
Brain MRI with contrast for every stage except IA — PET never substitutes for it
PET/CT for distant disease (or CT C/A/P + bone scan if unavailable)
Biopsy: EBUS, CT-guided transthoracic, metastatic site, or pleural cytology. Non-decalcified cores preferred for molecular

Pathologic mediastinal nodal evaluation for non-metastatic disease, especially stage II–III. EBUS reaches 2R/2L, 4R/4L, 7, 10, 11; mediastinoscopy cannot reach stations 5–6 (needs a Chamberlain procedure)
PD-L1 in every case. Molecular sequencing in all adenocarcinoma; add for squamous if never/light smoker, small biopsy, or adenosquamous
Stage IIIB or IV: concurrent tissue + liquid molecular testing (ctDNA ~7-day turnaround). A negative liquid biopsy does not rule out a driver — confirm on tissue

blocks.heading: Staging — TNM 9th (Jan 2025)
rows: ≤3 cm / >3–5 cm, or visceral pleura, adjacent lobe, or main bronchus
>5–7 cm or chest wall, phrenic nerve, same-lobe nodule / >7 cm or mediastinum, great vessels, carina, esophagus, spine, different ipsilateral lobe
Ipsilateral hilar (stations 10–14) / ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal — N2a single station, N2b multiple / contralateral or any supraclavicular
Pleural-pericardial effusion or nodules, or contralateral lung nodule / single extrathoracic met
Multiple mets, single organ system / multiple organ systems
blocks.footnote: What changed from the 8th edition: N2 split into N2a/N2b and M1c split into M1c1/M1c2. T descriptors are unchanged.

boxes: before any neoadjuvant therapy, at tumor board
systemic therapy if stage I >4 cm, stage II, stage III
omit IO if EGFR / ALK / RET / ROS1 altered
platinum doublet ×4, then IO if PD-L1 ≥1%
do not start systemic therapy until they return
IO before excluding a driver worsens outcomes
if severely symptomatic: 1–2 cycles platinum, then tailor
driver positive → targeted therapy, whatever the PD-L1
local consolidative therapy (SBRT or surgery) to all
sites, plus systemic therapy — improves PFS and OS

blocks.heading: Screening
items: USPSTF 2021 (Grade B): annual low-dose CT, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, currently smoking or quit within 15 years
Stop at 15 years since cessation, or when comorbidity would preclude curative surgery
NLST: 20% reduction in lung-cancer mortality vs chest radiography · NELSON: 24% in men (the women's subgroup did not reach significance)
Smoking cessation remains the highest-yield intervention — duration of smoking matters more than pack count

blocks.heading: Histology
rows: ~50%; peripheral, non/light smokers. TTF-1, napsin A, CK7 positive. Highest yield for actionable drivers. Mucinous (TTF-1−) is KRAS-enriched and EGFR-poor
~25%; central, cavitating, heavy smokers. CK5/6, p40 / p63; keratin pearls and intercellular bridges. Pemetrexed and bevacizumab are both contraindicated
Diagnosis of exclusion — treat as non-squamous
Both components, each ≥10% of the tumor

blocks.heading: Early stage — surgery and radiation
items: Lobectomy + mediastinal nodal sampling or dissection is the standard; VATS preferred over thoracotomy

Sublobar resection is acceptable for peripheral cT1aN0 ≤2 cm, after intraoperative nodal confirmation. CALGB 140503: non-inferior DFS (HR 1.01). JCOG0802: segmentectomy gave superior 5-yr OS (94.3% vs 91.1%) but doubled local relapse (10.5% vs 5.4%), and the survival gain came from non-lung-cancer deaths — read it as tolerability, not better cancer control
SBRT for medically inoperable stage I. Avoid central SBRT within 2 cm of the proximal bronchial tree
Preoperative assessment: predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO; <30% predicted flags high surgical risk

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — molecular drivers, resistance, and driver-negative disease

blocks.heading: Driver → therapy
rows: Osimertinib 80 mg daily (FLAURA). Add carbo/pemetrexed ×4 for higher-risk disease — CNS involvement, L858R, TP53 co-mutation (FLAURA2: mPFS 25.5 vs 16.7 mo; OS 47.5 vs 37.6). Or amivantamab + lazertinib (MARIPOSA: mPFS 23.7 vs 16.6 mo, HR 0.70; OS HR 0.75) — but grade ≥3 AEs 80% vs 52%, and it needs VTE prophylaxis for 4 months

Resistant to osimertinib and the classic TKIs. 1L amivantamab + carboplatin/pemetrexed (PAPILLON: mPFS 11.4 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40). Post-platinum: sunvozertinib (accelerated, 2L+ only). Mobocertinib was withdrawn in 2023

Lorlatinib 100 mg daily (CROWN: 5-yr PFS 60% vs 8% vs crizotinib, median not reached — the longest single-agent PFS reported in any solid tumor). Watch CNS effects (mood, cognition, seizures) and hyperlipidemia. Alternatives: alectinib, brigatinib, ensartinib

Four co-preferred 1L agents: crizotinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, taletrectinib. Prefer entrectinib / repotrectinib / taletrectinib if brain metastases — crizotinib has no CNS activity. Repotrectinib TKI-naive ORR 79%, mPFS 35.7 mo. Alectinib has no ROS1 activity despite its ALK potency

Selpercatinib — the only randomized 1L evidence (LIBRETTO-431: mPFS 24.8 vs 11.2 mo vs chemo ± pembrolizumab, HR 0.47; intracranial ORR 82%). Pralsetinib is an alternative with more pneumonitis. Watch hypertension and transaminitis
Capmatinib (1L ORR 68%) or tepotinib (1L ORR ~57%) — both single-arm, so those two numbers are not comparable. Tepotinib: watch peripheral edema
Encorafenib + binimetinib (PHAROS, treatment-naive ORR 75%) or dabrafenib + trametinib (ORR 64%, mPFS 10.9 mo). Pyrexia is the classic combination toxicity — hold and dose-modify

Not a first-line target — 1L is chemo-IO. 2L after platinum + anti-PD-(L)1: adagrasib (KRYSTAL-12: mPFS 5.5 vs 3.8 mo, HR 0.58) or sotorasib (CodeBreaK 200: 5.6 vs 4.5 mo, no OS difference; still on accelerated approval after a failed confirmatory filing — the weakest evidence base on this page)

Mostly exon 20 insertions; high rate of brain metastases at presentation. Zongertinib — oral, and as of Feb 2026 it carries a 1L indication (treatment-naive ORR 76%). T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3wk (DESTINY-Lung02: ORR 49%) — ILD in 13–15%, including fatal cases; monitor with serial imaging
Larotrectinib, entrectinib or repotrectinib — all tumor-agnostic approvals
Zenocutuzumab — accelerated approval, after progression on prior systemic therapy, for NSCLC and pancreatic adenocarcinoma only

blocks.heading: Progression on osimertinib
items: Rebiopsy — resistance is heterogeneous, with no single dominant mechanism
On-target: EGFR C797S. Off-target: MET amplification, HER2 amplification, acquired fusions
Histologic transformation is the one you cannot afford to miss: SCLC transformation (with RB1 and TP53 loss) or squamous transformation. Treat SCLC transformation as SCLC — platinum/etoposide
Standard next step is platinum-doublet chemotherapy
Amivantamab + chemotherapy (MARIPOSA-2: mPFS 6.3 vs 4.2 mo, HR 0.48). The approved regimen is amivantamab + chemo only — the lazertinib triplet was not approved, for excess hematologic toxicity
Datopotamab deruxtecan — TROP2 ADC on accelerated approval. The label is EGFR-mutant-specific: the all-comers trial met PFS but missed OS

blocks.heading: Driver-negative metastatic
items: PD-L1 ≥50%: pembrolizumab monotherapy (KEYNOTE-024: OS 30 vs 14 months); atezolizumab or cemiplimab are alternatives. Use chemo-IO instead if the burden is high or the patient is symptomatic
PD-L1 1–49% or <1%: chemo-IO doublet. Non-squamous → pembrolizumab + carboplatin + pemetrexed (KEYNOTE-189). Squamous → pembrolizumab + carboplatin + paclitaxel (KEYNOTE-407)
Dual IO — ipilimumab/nivolumab (CheckMate 227, 9LA) or durvalumab/tremelimumab (POSEIDON): chemo-sparing but more toxic, most attractive at PD-L1 <1% and in squamous
Second line: docetaxel 35 mg/m² days 1+8 — split dosing is better tolerated than 75 q3wk — ± ramucirumab

blocks.heading: Adjuvant therapy
items: Cisplatin doublet ×4 for stage II–IIIA (LACE: ~5% absolute 5-yr OS gain). Stage IB only if ≥4 cm or high-risk features; no benefit and possible harm in stage IA
EGFR → osimertinib ×36 months (ADAURA: DFS HR 0.17, OS HR 0.49). ALK → alectinib ×24 months (ALINA: DFS HR 0.24). Omit IO in both
Atezolizumab (IMpower010) is approved for stage II–IIIA with PD-L1 ≥1%, EGFR/ALK wild-type — but the 2025 update showed no significant OS benefit overall, with the signal concentrated at PD-L1 ≥50%
Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-091) after adjuvant chemotherapy, no PD-L1 restriction: DFS HR 0.76 overall — yet the PD-L1 ≥50% subgroup was not significant, the reverse of what you would predict

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, monitoring and trial evidence

blocks.heading: Perioperative and adjuvant dosing
rows: Cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² (or gemcitabine 1250 d1+8) + nivolumab 360 mg on day 1 — q21d ×3, then surgery
Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or gemcitabine 1000 d1+8) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → within 12 weeks, pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×13
Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or gemcitabine 1250 d1+8) + durvalumab 1500 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → durvalumab 1500 mg q28d ×12
Cisplatin 75 + pemetrexed 500 (or docetaxel 75) + nivolumab 360 mg q21d ×4 → surgery → within 90 days, nivolumab 360 mg q28d ×1 year
Cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 (non-squamous), gemcitabine 1250 d1+8, or docetaxel 75 — q21d ×4. Growth factor support if using docetaxel
Atezolizumab 1680 mg q4wk or pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk, after adjuvant chemotherapy

blocks.heading: Chemoradiation and metastatic dosing
rows: Carboplatin AUC 5 + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² q21d ×4, with daily RT
Cisplatin 50 mg/m² days 1, 8, 29, 36 + etoposide 50 mg/m² days 1–5 and 29–33; or carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 45 mg/m² weekly — with daily RT
10 mg/kg q14d ×12 months (or 1500 mg q4wk). Start within 6 weeks of finishing chemoRT
Carboplatin AUC 5–6 + pemetrexed 500 (non-squamous) or paclitaxel 200 (squamous) + pembrolizumab 200 mg q21d ×4 → pemetrexed + pembrolizumab maintenance
Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk (or 400 q6wk) · atezolizumab 1200 mg q3wk · cemiplimab 350 mg q3wk
Carboplatin AUC 6 + pemetrexed 500 q21d ×4, with osimertinib 80 mg daily continuously, then pemetrexed maintenance
Amivantamab weight-based (<80 kg 1050 mg, ≥80 kg 1400 mg) — split over days 1–2 in week 1, weekly through week 5, then q2wk from week 7; + lazertinib 240 mg PO daily. VTE prophylaxis ×4 months
35 mg/m² days 1+8 q21d — preferred over 75 q21d; reduce to 30 or 25 if heavily pretreated. ± ramucirumab 10 mg/kg

blocks.heading: Monitoring and cautions
items: Baseline HBsAg + anti-HBc before any immunosuppressive therapy; consider quantitative TB testing by risk
Pemetrexed: folic acid from ≥1 week before until 3 weeks after · B12 1000 mcg q9wk · dexamethasone 4 mg BID the day before and after, for rash. Never in squamous
Bevacizumab: contraindicated in squamous histology, significant hemoptysis, and large cavitary tumors. Urine protein every other cycle; treat hypertension
Cisplatin: avoid with hearing loss, CrCl <30, severe neuropathy, or poor performance status. Extensive hydration and aprepitant-containing antiemetics
Osimertinib: echo at baseline and q3 months ×6 months; ECG at baseline, 2 weeks, 6 weeks, and with any QT-prolonging drug
Alectinib: CK at baseline, 2 weeks, then q3 months · LFTs q2 weeks ×3 months. Lorlatinib: CNS effects and hyperlipidemia — median onset 15 days; rosuvastatin first-line
Immunotherapy: TSH and free T4 at baseline then q4–6 weeks. Prednisone 1–1.5 mg/kg for irAEs with a slow taper
Do not start a targeted agent — osimertinib and crizotinib above all — within 3 months of immunotherapy; the toxicity is additive. IO is also less effective in EGFR/ALK-driven disease

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Neoadjuvant platinum + nivolumab ×3 — pCR 24% vs 2%, EFS HR 0.63, OS HR 0.62
Perioperative pembrolizumab — EFS HR 0.58; the first perioperative IO trial with a confirmed OS benefit
Adjuvant osimertinib ×36 mo (DFS HR 0.17, OS HR 0.49) / alectinib ×24 mo (DFS HR 0.24)
Consolidation durvalumab after chemoRT — 5-yr OS 43% vs 33%
Consolidation osimertinib, EGFR-mutant stage III — PFS 39.1 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.16
Osimertinib 1L; adding chemo gives mPFS 25.5 vs 16.7 mo and OS 47.5 vs 37.6
Amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib — mPFS 23.7 vs 16.6 mo, OS HR 0.75, at a real toxicity cost
Amivantamab + chemo 1L for EGFR exon 20 — mPFS 11.4 vs 6.7 mo
Selpercatinib vs chemo ± pembrolizumab in RET — mPFS 24.8 vs 11.2 mo
Sublobar resection non-inferior for peripheral cT1aN0 ≤2 cm — DFS HR 1.01
